class_id: a repair rule that forbids arithmetic and mandates re-reading from source is unrunnable when most rows have no source left to re-read
feature: any data-repair or backfill policy written as 'never compute the corrected value, always re-derive it from the original source' — unit migrations, provenance repairs, re-extractions, currency or precision changes on historical rows
symptom: a safety rule is written after a real incident where a value was transformed blindly and became nonsense. The rule is correct about the failure it prevents, and it is stated absolutely: never arithmetic, always re-read from source. It is written while looking at the CODE PATH, where a source always exists because the row is being created from one. Nobody measures the EXISTING rows, where the source is a document that was purged under a retention policy, an endpoint that no longer serves a delisted entity, or a page that has changed. When the repair is finally built, it runs on the minority of rows that still have a source and, obeying the rule's own 'leave it alone and report it' clause, skips the rest. The column is then left holding BOTH the old and the new shape — strictly worse than before the repair, and precisely the mixed state the migration existed to avoid. The rule was not wrong; it was untested against the population it would have to run on. The generic test, cheap and available before any tool is written: join the rows the repair must touch against the source it names, and count how many actually have one.
first_seen: 2026-09-21 — IPODhan item 11 (OD-20 crore conversion), measured read-only on ipodhan_staging. The spec §5.2 says, in bold, 'Never by arithmetic on the stored number... The repair is a re-runnable tool that, per row, re-reads the value from its source (the offer document via the extractor, or the exchange payload); a row whose source cannot be re-read is left alone and reported, not guessed.' The rule is well-founded: it was written after a share count was once stored as a rupee amount. Measured against the 307 rows a conversion would touch (`issue_size > 0 AND segment IS NOT NULL`), only 46 have a COMPLETED extractable document (PRICE_BAND_AD / RHP / DRHP / PROSPECTUS) — 261 have none, 240 of those LISTED. A conforming tool would convert 15% of the column and report 85%. The source shortage has a documented cause that the rule's author also wrote: OD-32 purges document FILES after 7 days, so for older IPOs the document the repair would re-read is deliberately gone. Two rules, each sound alone, that cannot both be satisfied on the same rows. Separately measured and relevant to the resolution: no row in any of the five target columns holds a crore-shaped value, so the unit for this population is MEASURED rather than unknown — the condition the 'never' was protecting against does not currently hold.
fix_prs: none — escalated to the owner on #854 rather than resolved by a builder, because every path either relaxes a documented safety rule or commits operational cost. The three options recorded there: widen the source to the exchange payload (an operational call about re-fetching 261 mostly-LISTED IPOs); allow arithmetic where the unit is PROVABLY known, with the proof re-run as a precondition inside the tool (refuse to convert unless 100% of target rows are rupee-shaped in that run, so it fails closed the moment the data stops matching); or convert nothing and fix the readers instead, which is what #871 does for the two scorers. The general lesson is about ORDER, not about which option wins: measure the source's availability on the real population BEFORE writing a repair policy as an absolute, and state the measured coverage in the policy itself.
detection_check: none yet, and the right one is a policy-time check rather than a runtime one: any repair or backfill spec that names a source must carry the measured percentage of target rows for which that source is currently available, re-measured when the spec is used. A retention policy that deletes a source SHOULD name every repair path that reads it — OD-32 and this repair rule were written for the same system and never checked against each other. A cheap proxy for the runtime half: the tool reports converted / skipped counts and FAILS rather than exits 0 when skipped is non-zero, so a partial migration can never be mistaken for a completed one.
